Producer review feedback on CG-0MS934XSL00453HF (raised selection feature, currently in_review): when a card raises, the selection highlight does not raise with it. Additionally the raise slider should go to a maximum of 180px with a default of 60px.

Root cause: in HandView.updateSelectionTints(), applySelectionRaise(true) runs BEFORE the tint loop, so on first selection the raise tween starts before the tint overlay exists — the overlay is created at the resting position and is not in the tween targets, so the card raises while the highlight stays behind. Hover pointerover/pointerout also destroy+recreate the overlay, which can orphan it mid-tween.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Regression tests written FIRST (TDD): animated-path first-selection overlay is included in the raise tween targets; hover repaint reuses the overlay in place; reduced-motion first-selection overlay ends at the raised position.
2. The selection highlight overlay always ends at the raised position on first selection (animated and reduced-motion).
3. GymHandPileScene raise slider: RAISE_MAX = 180, RAISE_DEFAULT = 60; reset() restores the default; Controls help text updated.
4. HandView setSelectionLift() API default remains 0 (opt-in) — backward compatible.
5. npm run build succeeds and all HandView + Gym unit tests pass.

## Summary

Research spike to determine the client-side follow-detection mechanism for the "Follow us on Steam" incentive. The Steam client SDK has no direct "user follows this game's store page" call, so candidates must be verified before committing. This feature produces the decision-gate report that F4 depends on.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A report documents and evaluates each candidate: `ISteamFriends::IsFollowing(<developer account>)` (client-side, no backend), Steam Web API `IPlayerService` (game-page follow, needs server + publisher API key), and any other client-side candidates discovered.
- [ ] The report states a recommendation and flags the UX impact of each candidate (e.g. follows developer account vs game page).
- [ ] The recommendation is confirmed with the user (decision gate) and recorded in this item before F4 implementation commits to a mechanism.
- [ ] Any unknown (e.g. whether a server component is acceptable) is surfaced as an open question with options, not silently assumed.

## Minimal Implementation

- Prototype a minimal probe using the Steamworks SDK against a real Steam account (dev environment with Steam running).
- Research Steamworks SDK docs / community reports for `ISteamFriends::IsFollowing` semantics.
- Write findings to the work item as a structured report (markdown), including a decision recommendation.
- No production code committed in this feature.

## Prototype/Experiment

Success = a clear recommendation with evidence (docs/community/experiment) that the implementer can act on without re-research.

## Dependencies

- Parent blocked-by CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW (Electron launcher) — launcher must exist to run Steamworks in-app.

## Deliverables

- Decision-gate report (in work item comments).
- Confirmed mechanism choice.

# Staff job-applicant specialization mechanic

## Problem statement

Main Street currently has a single staff mechanic: staff cards that go into the player's hand and passively expand hand capacity (`handSlotsAdded`). There is no in-game staff that is employed at a specific deployed business and grants that business a passive specialization buff. This item adds that new staff mechanic.

## Users

- **Main Street player** — wants more meaningful decisions when hiring staff: choosing where to place an applicant, weighing passive buffs, and taking on per-turn salary costs.
- **Game designer** — wants a reusable, deterministic staff-applicant mechanic that works with existing staff templates and can be extended with new applicant cards later.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Applicant trigger:** Each turn there is a per-turn chance that a staff member applies for work at one of the deployed businesses on the street. The chance is computed as `(reputation + income per turn)%`, capped at 15%. The applicant targets a deployed business that has a free employment slot (one staff slot per business level).
2. **Passive specialization buff:** Each staff member grants a passive, always-on buff to the business at which they are employed. Skills are assigned from a specialization pool and are randomized **once per game** at game start, remaining locked for the full game; a staff member's skill is disconnected from its nominal job (e.g. a "Baker" can carry a "Town Gossip" skill). At a minimum the "Town Gossip" skill is implemented, firing the existing once-per-turn peek mechanic (see CG-0MSXOW6GN008ZSMN).
3. **Hire / decline flow:** The applicant is presented as a new card type that **walks on from the left** of the screen. The player either lets it walk off to the right (decline) or hires it (walks into the hand / is employed). Hiring costs **no immediate coins** but adds an ongoing per-turn salary cost (deducted alongside existing staff/community-space ongoing costs during the income phase, clamped at 0 coins).
4. **Capacity & let-go economics:** A business can employ one staff member per business level (level 1 = 1 slot, etc.). The player can let a staff member go (lay off), which costs 1 turn's salary and 1 reputation.
5. **Tests & docs:** The mechanic is covered by unit tests (deterministic trigger under seeded RNG, passive-buff application, hire/decline, let-go penalties, per-level slot enforcement) and a browser/scene test for the walk-on/walk-off presentation. All related documentation is updated (code comments, README/wiki docs entries as applicable). Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Staff applicants for this mechanic are **distinct** from the existing hand-slot staff cards (`handSlotsAdded` mechanic) — they do not go into the player's hand as hand cards; they are employed at a deployed business.
- Applicant pool starts from existing staff templates; add new applicant cards via the follow-up work item CG-0MT1CIWSD003VBPK (not scope here).
- Passive buffs are applied per-business; must not conflict with existing per-slot `currentIncome` / `currentReputationPerTurn` caching in `applyIncome`.
- New card presentation must follow SLL positioning and the shared HandView/PileView / animation + SFX conventions per AGENTS.md (rule 8, `COMMON_SFX_KEYS`, reduced-motion respected).

## Existing state

- `StaffCard` interface in `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCards.ts` (familly: 'staff') with `handSlotsAdded`, `reputationPerTurn`, `refreshCostDiscount`, `actionsPerTurn`. Staff templates loaded from `card-data.csv` (`_STAFF_CARD_TEMPLATES`).
- `MainStreetState.ts`: `streetGrid` of deployed businesses/community-spaces; `staffCards[]` (hand-slot staff) + `staffCardMarket[]`; business cards carry `maxLevel`/`level`.
- `MainStreetEngine.ts`: `hireStaffCard()` (hand-slot hire), `layOffStaffCard()` (hand-slot layoff), `executeDayStart()` resets per-turn state; `applyIncome()` in `MainStreetAdjacency.ts` deducts staff + community-space ongoing costs and applies per-slot income/rep.
- Related peek skill work: CG-0MSXOW6GN008ZSMN (implement staff peek skill), CG-0MSXOWLHU0099QF6 (face-down deck rendering).

## Desired change

Introduce a per-turn staff-applicant phase/step in the turn loop: roll the applicant chance, when triggered pick a deployed business with a free employment slot and spawn an applicant card that walks on from the left. On hire, employ the applicant at that business, add its passive specialization buff to the business's income/rep/synergy computations, and register its ongoing salary cost. On decline, walk the card off to the right with no effect. Add per-level employment-slot tracking, and a let-go action costing 1 turn's salary + 1 reputation.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetState.ts` — new state: applicant presentation state, per-business employment slots, employed-applicant list.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts` — new applicant-trigger step, hire/decline/let-go actions, ongoing-cost integration; `resolveIncident`-style applicant chance roll.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAdjacency.ts` — apply passive specialization buffs per-business in `applyIncome` (+ currentReputationPerTurn).
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCards.ts` — applicant/specialization skill type definitions (start with existing templates + Town Gossip skill).
- `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv` — Town Gossip skill / any new specialization columns if added.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetRenderer.ts` + `MainStreetAnimator.ts` — new card type walk-on (from left) / walk-off (right) / walk-into-hand animation + SFX.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` / `MainStreetCommands.ts` — hire/decline input + command wiring.
- `tests/main-street/` — unit + browser tests for the mechanic.

## Related work

- CG-0MSXOW6GN008ZSMN — Implement staff peek skill ("Town Gossip" active peek).
- CG-0MSXOXN81004MW8I — Add peek once-per-turn unit tests.
- CG-0MT1CIWSD003VBPK — Staff specialization: new applicant card suggestions (follow-up, out of scope here).
- CG-0MSQJ7VL9009JHF4 — Group F: Staff abilities beyond hand slots.
- CG-0MS9HJ6AL0087DPB — Engine: ongoingCost for community spaces (same ongoing-cost deduction path).

## Clarifying questions & answers (Appendix)

- Q: How frequently does a staff member apply? — Answer (producer): Per-turn chance computed as `(reputation + income per turn)%`, capped at 15%. Source: interactive reply 2026-08-20, recorded in comment CG-C0MT1CHYML001OOU8.
- Q: Are specializations passive or active? — Answer (producer): Passive, always-on buff applied to the business at which they are employed. Source: interactive reply 2026-08-20.
- Q: When is the specialization randomized? — Answer (producer): Once per game at start, locked for the full game. Source: interactive reply 2026-08-20.
- Q: Which staff pool for applicants? — Answer (producer): Start with existing staff templates; create a follow-up work item for new card suggestions. → Created CG-0MT1CIWSD003VBPK. Source: interactive reply 2026-08-20.
- Q: How is the applicant presented in the UI? — Answer (producer): New card type that walks on from the left, then either walks off to the right (decline) or walks into the hand (hire). Source: interactive reply 2026-08-20.
- Q: What is the specific applicant trigger rate? — Answer (producer): `(Reputation + income per turn)%` capped at 15%. Open detail: the "Town Gossip" example in the original description describes an *active* peek to the top 3 cards of the upcoming deck, which conflicts with the producer's "passive" answer — resolved as passive buff with the active peek delegated to the existing peek skill (CG-0MSXOW6GN008ZSMN). Source: interactive reply 2026-08-20 + item description.

---

## Related work (automated report — find_related)

- **CG-0MLSDXY9F1FSGQ38** – Coloretto (set-building tableau) (completed)
- **CG-0MSRGUM4P009XRM3** – Upgrade level-up burst on target business (completed)
- **CG-0MSTB03U6009J2WV** – Main Street: clicking a tutorial button should not pass through to the cards below (completed)
- Repo file matches: `.worklog/worktrees/wl-CG-0MSXIQDI4007K6N0-hud-2dp/docs/DEVELOPER.md`, `.worklog/worktrees/wl-CG-0MSXOW6GN008ZSMN-peek/docs/DEVELOPER.md` (contextual).

# Speed up browser tests and create test profiles

**Priority: Medium** | **Type: Task**

> Browser tests take ~15 min (92 files). Profile: smoke (30s), dev (3 min), ci (full). Remove low-value tests (27 reduced-motion variants, redundant gym smokes).

## Current State

- 92 browser test files across 14 directories
- Total runtime: ~12-15 minutes (non-tutorial browser tests)
- isolate: true + fileParallelism: false = fresh browser per file, sequential
- Per-game timing: Main Street ~146s (24 files), Golf ~64s, Gym ~42s, Beleaguered Castle ~49s

## Problems

1. Browser launch overhead dominates: fresh Chromium per file + Phaser boot
2. Sequential execution blocks fast tests on slow ones
3. 27 reduced-motion variants across 10 files - duplicate assertions with animation disabled
4. Gym tests (19 files) check rendering/boots, not game play
5. No test profiles - developers wait 15 min for feedback

## Proposed Solution

### 1. Three Test Profiles

- smoke: 1 file/game (8 files) - ~30s - rapid feedback during implementation
- dev: Smoke + key E2E per game (~25 files) - ~3 min - implement/audit workflow
- ci: All 92 files - ~5-6 min - CI (after cleanup)

### 2. Remove Low-Value Tests (27 tests, 10 files)

Reduced-motion variants that duplicate main test assertions:
- incident-reveal.browser.test.ts - 7 reduced-motion variants
- click-place.browser.test.ts - 3 reduced-motion variants
- market-deal-in.browser.test.ts - 4 reduced-motion variants
- sell-demolition.browser.test.ts - 4 reduced-motion variants
- event-played.browser.test.ts - 4 reduced-motion variants
- synergy-formation.browser.test.ts - 3 reduced-motion variants
- upgrade-level-up.browser.test.ts - 2 reduced-motion variants
- day-banner.browser.test.ts - 3 reduced-motion variants
- income-collection.browser.test.ts - 3 reduced-motion variants

### 3. Optimizations

a) Merge reduced-motion variants into parent tests
b) Share game instances within test files (reduce game boots via beforeEach)
c) Reduce gym from 19 files to 1 smoke + 1 feature file
d) Tutorial E2E tests (7 files) excluded from smoke/dev profiles

### 4. Implementation Steps

1. Create run-smoke-tests.sh / run-dev-tests.sh with vitest project filters
2. Remove reduced-motion variant tests (27 tests)
3. Merge remaining tests to share game instances
4. Reduce gym tests
5. Update package.json scripts
6. Update docs/DEVELOPER.md

## Key Files

- vite.config.ts: vitest browser test configuration (isolate, fileParallelism, timeout)
- package.json: test scripts (add test:smoke, test:dev)
- scripts/run-ci-tests.sh: CI test runner (add smoke/dev stages)
- tests/**/*.browser.test.ts: browser test files to review for removal

# Upgrade cards: consume an action and go to hand first (drag-drop = buy & play same turn)

## Plan Changelog

**2026-08-22**: Plan created (7 child work items, test-first ordering, Medium effort/Medium risk).

## Plan Summary

This work item decomposes the upgrade economy fix into 7 child tasks with test-first ordering:

### Phase 1: Unit Tests (test-first, no dependencies)
- **CG-0MT407BKP000J4N9** — Unit tests: upgrade action economy

### Phase 2: Core Engine Wiring (parallel with browser tests)
- **CG-0MT40APW6003MSCT** — Engine: wire action cost into upgrade commands

### Phase 3: Implementation (3 parallel tracks)
- **CG-0MT40EHB1005JP6D** — Engine: implement hand-first click flow + target selection
- **CG-0MT40FT21005GBK7** — Engine: implement drag-drop buy-and-play
- **CG-0MT40HTYN008TJ6Q** — AI and Monte Carlo: budget-aware upgrade actions

### Browser Tests (test-first, parallel with implementation)
- **CG-0MT40CNO1002MSDC** — Browser tests: hand-first click flow for upgrades
- **CG-0MT40GTSU006C6U1** — Browser tests: drag-drop and premium for upgrades

### Phase 4: Integration & Polish
- **CG-0MT42HHAB000VJUK** — Update existing tests, E2E, and documentation

### Dependency Graph
```
CG-0MT407BKP000J4N9 (unit tests)
       |
       v
CG-0MT40APW6003MSCT (engine: action cost)
    /      |       \
   v       v        v
CG-0MT40EHB1005JP6D  CG-0MT40FT21005GBK7  CG-0MT40HTYN008TJ6Q
(hand-first flow)    (drag-drop)           (AI/MC)
       \                |                /
        \               |               /
         v              v              v
        CG-0MT42HHAB000VJUK (update tests/E2E/docs)

CG-0MT40CNO1002MSDC (browser: hand flow) ---\
CG-0MT40GTSU006C6U1 (browser: drag-drop) ----/
       |
       +-- blocks respective implementation children
```

## Problem statement

Playing an upgrade card currently costs **no action** and never passes through the hand — a market upgrade click applies the upgrade directly to the first eligible business (`buyUpgradeCommand` → `purchaseUpgrade`, no `consumeAction()`). This diverges from the business-card economy (move-to-hand = 1 action, same-day place free, held-card play = 1 action, drag-drop buy-and-place = 1 action + 50% premium) and gives upgrade cards a free second daily action. Upgrades should behave like business cards: go to the hand first when bought by click, with drag-and-drop as the same-turn buy-and-play path.

## Users

- **As a player**, I want playing an upgrade card to consume one of my daily actions like every other purchase/play **so that** the action economy stays honest (1 action/day, 2 with General Manager) and upgrades aren't a free lunch.
- **As a player**, I want upgrades I buy to land in my hand first **so that** I can choose when and where to apply them (target a specific business, possibly next day).
- **As a player**, I want to drag an upgrade straight from the market onto a business when I'm sure **so that** I can buy-and-play in one turn at a +50% premium, exactly like business buy-and-place.
- **As a player**, I want to pick which business to upgrade when playing from hand **so that** I can respond to my current street layout (e.g. branches / multi-level chains).

## Acceptance Criteria (Parent)

- [ ] **Action cost — click path:** Clicking a market upgrade moves it to hand and consumes 1 action; playing the same-day moved upgrade applies it with no additional action; playing a held-from-previous-day upgrade consumes 1 action. All paths decrement actionsRemaining and legality gates reject the action when the budget is spent.
- [ ] **Hand-first + target selection:** Upgrade market cards follow the two-step hand flow — never applied directly from the market on click. When an upgrade is selected in hand, the player clicks an eligible business on the street to apply it; ineligible targets are rejected with illegal-move feedback.
- [ ] **Drag-drop same-turn:** Upgrades in the market are draggable onto eligible street businesses — drag-drop = buy & play in the same turn, consumes 1 action, and charges the +50% premium. Illegal drops snap back with feedback.
- [ ] **Free ops unchanged:** Event cards' free move-to-hand and free play stay free; refresh, sell, hint, discard, community favour, end-turn remain non-action operations.
- [ ] **AI + Monte Carlo:** MainStreetAiStrategy and MainStreetMonteCarlo account for the upgrade action cost in budget-aware valuation, and remain deterministic per seed.
- [ ] **Testing/validation:** New unit tests cover action spend + gating for all three upgrade paths; browser tests cover the hand-first click flow, drag-drop onto eligible/illegal targets, and action-budget dimming; existing upgrade tests updated to the new flow.
- [ ] **Docs:** All related documentation updated; full project test suite (npm test) and npm run build pass.

## Constraints

- Preserve the existing action economy: 1 action/day (2 with General Manager) — upgrades must not create a second implicitly-free action.
- Same-day composite stays free (consistency with business cards); the 50% premium formula must match the business buy-and-place exactly.
- Undo/redo must wrap the new paths (snapshotted commands; new actions after undo invalidate the redo stack).
- State/transcript/save-load fields must stay consistent (e.g. justMovedHandCardId semantics generalise to upgrades; pendingUpgradeIndex-style state added if needed).
- Reduced-motion and mute settings must be respected by any new animation/SFX.

## Effort and Risk

- **Effort:** Medium (37.83h recommended, range [26h-57h])
- **Risk:** Medium (score 10/25, confidence 74%)

Unit tests: upgrade action economy

**Priority: High** | **Type: Task** | **Parent: CG-0MT3IYSRL001VVUP**

## Problem statement

Before implementing the upgrade action economy changes, we need unit tests that verify the action-spend behavior for all three upgrade paths. These tests will fail initially (red) and pass after implementation (green), providing regression coverage.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Test move-to-hand action cost: `moveToHandCommand` for upgrade cards calls `consumeAction()` and decrements `actionsRemaining`. Test that when `actionsRemaining <= 0`, the command fails with appropriate legality error.
- Test same-day composite free: When an upgrade was moved to hand same-turn via `moveToHandCommand`, `playUpgradeFromHandCommand` does NOT consume a second action (same-day composite). Test verifies `actionsRemaining` unchanged after play.
- Test held-card play costs action: When an upgrade was held from a previous day (not same-day), `playUpgradeFromHandCommand` consumes 1 action. Test verifies `actionsRemaining` decremented.
- Test drag-drop premium: `buyAndPlaceUpgradeCommand` consumes 1 action and charges the +50% premium (`Math.ceil(cost * 1.5 * 2) / 2`). Test verifies both action cost and premium amount.
- Test legality gating: All upgrade paths reject when `actionsRemaining <= 0`. Test covers click path, hand-play path, and drag-drop path.
- Test free ops unchanged: Event cards' free move-to-hand and free play stay free (no action consumed); refresh, sell, hint, discard, community favour, end-turn remain non-action operations.
- Existing unit tests pass: All existing tests in `tests/main-street/` continue to pass.

## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCommands.ts` — `buyUpgradeCommand`, `playUpgradeFromHandCommand`, `buyAndPlaceUpgradeCommand`
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts` — `executeAction` action handling
- `tests/main-street/upgrade-action-economy.test.ts` — new test file

## Dependencies

- Depends on: none (test-first, written before implementation)
- Blocks: next child item (Engine: wire action cost into upgrade commands)

## Deliverables

- New test file `tests/main-street/upgrade-action-economy.test.ts` with failing tests for all 6 ACs
- Tests pass after implementation of F-1 through F-3

## Problem statement

`npm run monte-carlo` (and `monte-carlo-sweep`) fails with `ERR_UNKNOWN_FILE_EXTENSION` because `tsx` does not understand Vite's `?raw` query suffix used to import `card-data.csv` in `MainStreetCards.ts`.

## Users

- **TCE developer** running Monte Carlo balance analysis: expects `npm run monte-carlo` to produce `results/main-street-monte-carlo.json` and `.csv`.
- **CI/automated tooling** (future): may run the harness headlessly.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `npm run monte-carlo -- --seeds 200 --seed-prefix mc-balance --maxTurns 25 --strategy greedy --out results/main-street-monte-carlo.json --csv-out results/main-street-monte-carlo.csv` completes successfully (exit 0) and produces valid output files.
2. `npm run monte-carlo-sweep -- --sweep --seeds 100 --seed-prefix mc-balance --maxTurns 25 --out results/sweep.json --csv-out results/sweep.csv` completes successfully (exit 0).
3. `npm run build` succeeds (TypeScript + Vite production build).
4. Full test suite `npm test` passes.

## Constraints

- The fix should use `vite-node` (already proven to work; documented in `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` line 67).
- Per the Doc-Update Policy, `docs/DEVELOPER.md` and `AGENTS.md` scripts list must be updated if scripts change.
- Do not modify `tsx` or add loader hooks — that is more fragile and less established.

## Existing state

- `scripts/monte-carlo.ts` imports Main Street game code which uses `import cardDataRaw from './card-data.csv?raw';`
- `package.json` defines `monte-carlo` and `monte-carlo-sweep` scripts using `tsx`.
- `vite-node` works for the same import (used by `scripts/generate-main-street-expanded-card-manifest.ts`).

## Desired change

Switch `monte-carlo` and `monte-carlo-sweep` npm scripts in `package.json` from `tsx` to `vite-node`. Update documentation (DEVELOPER.md, AGENTS.md) to reflect the change.

## Key Files

- `package.json` — Change `monte-carlo` and `monte-carlo-sweep` script commands.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — Update script listings to reflect `vite-node` usage.
- `AGENTS.md` — Update scripts list to reflect `vite-node` usage.

## Related work

- Discovered from: CG-0MT47FBLS000E7PW (Monte Carlo sanity check)
- Sibling pattern: `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` line 67 documents `vite-node` usage for a similar import path.
- Pre-existing: reproduced at commit b2bec26b before CG-0MT3J8FXG006RCOA F1-F4 work.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Why not fix tsx instead of switching to vite-node?" — Answer: tsx does not support Vite `?raw` queries natively; adding a loader hook is fragile and unmaintainable. vite-node is the established pattern in this repo (see `generate-main-street-expanded-card-manifest.ts`). Source: code review of `MainStreetCards.ts` and `card-catalog.md`.
- Q: "Are there other `tsx` scripts that might also break on `?raw` imports?" — Answer: No — `scripts/monte-carlo.ts` and `scripts/replay.ts` and `scripts/export-transcripts.ts` are the only scripts using `tsx`. # Events in Main Street should be paid for when executed

**Status: Feature already implemented.** This work item was auto-completed during intake because the requested feature was already implemented by CG-0MM8U3SVW1SD1E9P on 2026-03-01.

## Original Request

In Main Street, businesses are taken to the hand for free and paid for when executed. Events should be treated the same way on both counts:
1. Taken to hand for free (already the case)
2. Paid for when executed (already implemented)

## Finding: Already Done

**CG-0MM8U3SVW1SD1E9P** ("Fix incident queue alignment, add investment costs, and remove auto-play of held investments") — completed 2026-03-01 — already implemented cost-at-play for Investment event cards:

- `playEventFromHand()` in `MainStreetMarket.ts` (line 597) deducts `event.cost` from `state.resourceBank.coins` before resolving effects.
- `EventCard` interface includes a `cost: number` field used at play time.
- Test `tests/main-street/refresh-market.test.ts` ("charges an event card when played from hand (cost-at-play)") confirms coin deduction.
- Incident events have `cost: 0` by design (auto-drawn, not purchased).

## Per-Turn Holding Cost

The description mentions an "open work item will add a per turn cost to holding a card in the hand." This was handled by **CG-0MTC31LN3000UHDY** ("Don't charge for businesses held in the hand") which **reversed** the ongoing-cost deduction for hand-held businesses. By consistent treatment, events also do not incur per-turn costs while in hand.

## Related Work

- **CG-0MT5W4V98000EDOO** "Executing an event in Main Street consumes an action" — open, idea stage. Complementary: events cost coins but currently do NOT consume an action. This is the remaining gap in event economics.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Investment events charge `event.cost` coins when played from hand (CG-0MM8U3SVW1SD1E9P).
- [x] Incident events have `cost: 0` by design (auto-drawn).
- [x] Hand-held cards (business + events) do not incur per-turn costs (CG-0MTC31LN3000UHDY).
- [x] Full test suite passes.

## Goal (user story)

As a Main Street player, I want to play a competitive mode against an AI opponent who builds businesses on the **same street**, so that turns give me more to do and the game has a rival to race against.

## Design scope (from feasibility analysis, 2025-07 session)

- **Shared street grid** (10 slots); each placed business is owned by one player; income from a business accrues to its **owner**.
- **Events affect the whole street**: investment events and incidents keep the existing street-wide resolution semantics, but income/damage must be routed per-owner.
- **Staff are player-only**: the AI does not hire staff, and its competitive decision space excludes staff actions (hire-staff, peek).
- **Single shared market row**: buying a card denies it to the opponent (market competition is a first-class feature).
- **Alternating turn structure** — design decision to confirm at intake: alternate MarketPhases within a shared day vs. alternating full days.

## Reusability findings (basis for this item)

- The decision layer (`MainStreetAiStrategy`, `GreedyStrategy`, `scoreAction`, `enumerateLegalActions`, `MainStreetAiPlayer`) transfers ~1:1 — it is UI-free and already shared between the Monte Carlo harness and the hint system.
- The state/engine layers are single-owner: `MainStreetState` has one resourceBank/hand/staffCards/actionsRemaining; `applyIncome`, `resolveEvent`, `resolveIncident`, `computeScore`, `checkEndConditions` all assume one owner. These need a per-player split plus owner-tagged grid slots.
- Greedy heuristics assume the AI owns the whole street (`scoreBusinessAction = (income+synergy)*horizon - cost`; `aiPlanningHorizon` reads a single score) — scoring must become ownership-aware.
- PRD M3 (`docs/main-street/prd-milestone-3.md`) explicitly scoped "AI vs. player (competitive mode)" as N/A — this item is a deliberate scope extension; note it in the PRD.

## Acceptance criteria (proposed)

- AC1: A competitive-mode state model exists with per-player coins/reputation, hand, staff, action budget and score, plus owner-tagged street slots; deterministic and replayable via seeded RNG.
- AC2: The AI opponent plays a legal full turn through the existing strategy layer (`enumerateLegalActions` → scored choice → `executeAction`), with staff actions excluded.
- AC3: Income accrues to the owner of each business; street-wide events/incidents affect both players under the shared-street semantics.
- AC4: A head-to-head Monte Carlo harness (extending `MainStreetMonteCarlo`) measures the win distribution across >=200 seeds to validate competitive balance.
- AC5 (scene, may be split into a child at planning): competitive mode is selectable from the game selector, renders the shared street with owner colouring, alternates turns, and animates AI turns with SFX per the audio/feedback rule (AGENTS.md best practice 8).
data.title: Main Street competitive mode: AI opponent on the shared street

## Goal (user story)

As a developer of the competitive mode, I want the balancing AI's decision layer (`MainStreetAiStrategy` / `GreedyStrategy` / `scoreAction` / `MainStreetAiPlayer`) adapted to shared-street competitive semantics, so the opponent plays competently on a street it does not fully own.

## Context

The existing heuristics assume the AI owns the whole street:
- `scoreBusinessAction` / `scorePlayBusinessFromHandAction` value `(income + synergy) * horizon - cost` with no ownership concept.
- `aiPlanningHorizon` measures distance to the win threshold via `computeScore`, which sums a single player's coins + reputation.
- `enumerateLegalActions` includes staff actions (`hire-staff`, `peek-incident-deck`) — competitive mode makes staff player-only.

Parent: Main Street competitive mode epic (CG-0MT5X3GMA007EG30).

## Scope

- Ownership-aware scoring: evaluate income, synergy, and horizon against the **AI's own** resources/businesses and its own win threshold.
- Staff exclusion: competitive-mode action enumeration drops staff actions from the AI's option space.
- Deterministic validation: extend `MainStreetMonteCarlo` (or a sibling harness) to run head-to-head AI-vs-AI and, where feasible, AI-vs-baseline matches across >=200 seeds; document win/score distributions.

## Out of scope (decision to record in item)

Whether to add opponent-aware *denial* reasoning (blocking the opponent's best slot, buying to deny) — record an explicit in/out decision with rationale; denial can be a follow-up child if in.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: `scoreAction` and the per-type scoring helpers evaluate placement/upgrade/event value using only the acting player's resources and owned businesses, with the planning horizon computed from the acting player's own score vs. their win threshold.
- AC2: Competitive-mode legal-action enumeration excludes `hire-staff` and staff-skill actions (peek), while the shared single-player enumeration is unchanged.
- AC3: A deterministic head-to-head Monte Carlo harness runs the adapted strategy against a baseline over >=200 seeds and produces win/score distribution metrics (extension of `MainStreetMonteCarloMetrics` or equivalent).
- AC4: All existing single-player AI tests (ai-strategy, hint consistency, balance guardrails) still pass unchanged.

# Intake Brief: Wellness Fair should act on Health businesses

## Problem statement

The Wellness Fair event card (`evt-wellness-fair`) in Main Street currently targets **Service** businesses — granting "+2 coins per Service business and +1 reputation." It should target **Health** businesses instead, which is thematically consistent (a wellness fair benefits health businesses) and aligns with the Health synergy group.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Wellness Fair targets Health businesses** — In `card-data.csv`, `targetSynergy` for `evt-wellness-fair` changed from `Service` to `Health`.
2. **Effect description updated** — The `effect` column text updated from "+2 coins per Service business and +1 reputation." to "+2 coins per Health business and +1 reputation." (or "+2 coins per Health business and +1.5 reputation." if the reputationDelta of 1.5 is intentional — operator to confirm).
3. **Card catalog documentation updated** — `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` updated to reflect Health as the target synergy (replacing Service).
4. **No test changes needed** — No existing tests reference `evt-wellness-fair` or `Wellness Fair`, so the change is purely data/documentation.
5. **Full project test suite passes** — all unit tests, browser tests, and E2E tutorials pass with no regressions.

## Constraints

- This is a single-card data change — scope is limited to `evt-wellness-fair` in `card-data.csv` and the card catalog documentation.
- Must not affect other event cards (Block Party → Entertainment, Grand Opening Sale → Commerce, Charity Drive → All).
- The `resolveEvent` engine logic for `SpecificSynergy` remains unchanged; it simply reads `targetSynergy` from the card data.

## Existing state

| Field | Current value |
|---|---|
| `targetSynergy` | `Service` |
| `effect` | "+2 coins per Service business and +1 reputation." |
| `coinDelta` | 2 |
| `reputationDelta` | 1.5 |
| `target` | SpecificSynergy |
| `tier` | 3 (Neighborhood) |
| `trigger` | Investment |

## Desired change

| Field | Current value | New value |
|---|---|---|
| `targetSynergy` | `Service` | `Health` |
| `effect` | "+2 coins per Service business and +1 reputation." | "+2 coins per Health business and +1 reputation." (pending repDelta confirmation) |
| Card catalog | "Service" in synergy column | "Health" |

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv` — Change `targetSynergy` from `Service` to `Health` for `evt-wellness-fair`; update effect text
- `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` — Update the Wellness Fair row to reflect Health as the target synergy

## Related work

- **CG-0MSXIS2QI002WMKR** — "Main Street: Free Health Screening grants reputation only (no coins)" — parallel fix for a Health-synergy event card (completed).
- **CG-0MSQJ7SYD008U3EE** — "Group E: Upgrade cards — cover new businesses (12 cards)" — introduced upgrade cards for Day Spa and Yoga Studio (Health-synergy businesses).

---

## Appendix: Clarifying questions

- *Q: Should the `effect` text reflect the actual reputationDelta of 1.5 ("+1.5 reputation") or round to "+1 reputation"?* — Answer: **+1 reputation** (round down for display). The 1.5 value in the CSV appears to be a pre-existing discrepancy between the displayed effect text and the raw data. The fix keeps the displayed effect consistent ("+1 reputation") while the raw delta of 1.5 is preserved to avoid unintended balance changes. If the operator intends to also fix the 1.5 → 1 discrepancy, that should be a separate work item.
- *Q: Are there any Health-synergy businesses currently in the game that would make this change impactful?* — Answer: **Yes.** Day Spa (`biz-day-spa`) and Yoga Studio (`biz-yoga-studio`) both have Health as one of their synergy types, so the change will meaningfully affect gameplay for Health-focused builds.
